clinician.trajectory_summary: A 23-year-old female with allergic asthma and GERD presented with nausea, vomiting, and abdominal pain. Initial workup including MRCP was negative, and she was started on pantoprazole and metoclopramide. Over the subsequent 3-month follow-up, she developed acute kidney injury with serum creatinine initially rising to 2.2 mg/dL, transiently improving to 1.8 mg/dL, but then re-peaking at 2.5 mg/dL during conservative management despite discontinuation of pantoprazole. Urinalysis revealed proteinuria of 900 mg/dL. Renal biopsy demonstrated marked interstitial infiltrate with tubulitis, focal tubular epithelial cell necrosis, and an admixture of eosinophils with T-cell predominant infiltrate. Concurrently, she developed bilateral eye redness over 8-9 days, and ophthalmologic examination confirmed anterior uveitis with keratic precipitates and posterior synechiae bilaterally, with visual acuity declining from 20/20 to 20/30-2 (right) and 20/20-2 (left). Extensive autoimmune serologic workup (ANCA, anti-dsDNA, anti-SSA/B, anti-Smith, cryoglobulins, complement) was negative. She was treated with systemic prednisone 60 mg daily tapered over months and topical prednisolone acetate, resulting in normalization of serum creatinine to 1.0 mg/dL and restoration of visual acuity to baseline.
